additionalInformation.description: Carefully assess the necessity of sharing personal data and ensure that the involved parties genuinely require access to that data.

impact.description: In addition to legal implications (non-compliance), this also raises the likelihood and impact of theft, data leaks, and unwanted or accidental disclosure to unintended parties. The more data is disclosed to and by the system, the more likely it can be abused for detecting, linking, identifying, or non-repudiation threats by any of the threat sources considered.

additionalInformation.description: Disclosures should consider the best interests of the involved data subjects, with the minimization principle playing a crucial role. The system should be designed to only collect, process, store, and share the minimum amount of personal data necessary for the required functionality.

threatType.name: Unawareness and Unintervenability
threatType.description: Unawareness and unintervenability threats occur when individuals are insufficiently informed, involved, or empowered with respect to the processing of their personal data.
threatType.fullDescription:
This threat category focuses on the lack of support offered to the involved or affected individuals. Evaluating a system in terms of unawareness threats involves assessing the privacy harm caused by the system on a data subject by insufficiently informing, involving, or empowering the data subject in its role and relation to the system.
These threats capture three potential lacks of system support: (i) not properly informing data subjects about the collection of data and what is going on with that data in the system (lack of transparency), (ii) insufficiently making users that provide the system with personal data (about themselves or others) aware of the potential privacy harm or impact (lack of user feedback), and (iii) not providing data subjects with the required controls or means to influence how their data are being handled.

characteristic.name: Unawareness as data subject
characteristic.description: Unawareness of processing focuses on data subjects not being aware about the collection, processing, storage, or disclosure of their personal data.
characteristic.fullDescription: This focuses on unawareness of the types of processing.

characteristicExample.name: Third parties
characteristicExample.description: Data subjects are not aware of the identities of the third parties with whom their data will be shared.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: Websites may share personal data to a number of different third parties without disclosing to the data subject who those parties are.

characteristicExample.name: Notice unclear
characteristicExample.description: The privacy notice provided to the data subject was not presented in clear and plain language.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: The explanation provided to the data subject about which personal data is processed and why, may be vague and ambiguously worded.

characteristicExample.name: Unawareness of data collected by traffic cams
characteristicExample.description: Data subjects are unaware that traffic cameras collect not only number plates but also facial images.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: The data subject is unaware of the amount of personal data that is collected, processed, by traffic cameras. For example, these cameras could also perform number plate recognition or face recognition, or attempt to determine whether drivers are using their phones.

characteristicExample.name: Unawareness about collection of news consumption data
characteristicExample.description: Data subjects are unaware that their newspaper uses usage data for targeted advertising purposes.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: While a user has to login to a news site to which they have a paid subscription, they may be unaware that the site also collects usage data for personalization and targeted advertising purposes.

characteristicExample.name: Unaware of indirect collection for extensive profiling
characteristicExample.description: The data subject is unaware that their personal data is collected from third parties to construct more detailed user profiles for targeted advertising (e.g., Facebook).
characteristicExample.fullDescription: While the user may be aware that a site builds a profile for targeted advertising, they may not be aware of how the site also indirectly gathers data from many different third party organizations in order to build a more elaborate profile.

characteristicExample.name: Marketing purpose
characteristicExample.description: The data subject is unaware the data may also be used for marketing purposes.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: A data subject may provide certain data to a website to register for an account and access a service, they may be unaware that the data is also used for marketing purposes.

characteristicExample.name: Purpose/retention
characteristicExample.description: The data subject was not informed why or for how long their personal data is processed.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: A site may mention the data that is processed, but omits to inform its users on why and for how long their data is going to be processed.

impact.name: Unaware of data usage
impact.description: Insufficient transparency may lead to data subjects being unaware that their personal data is utilized for certain purposes, especially if those purposes are different from what was initially indicated.
impact.fullDescription: The data subject is unaware that their personal data is used for certain processing purposes. These purposes may be incompatible with the reason for sharing the personal data in the first place.

criteria.name: Data subject unaware
criteria.description: Are data subjects insufficiently informed about the processing of personal data, including the purposes and methods of the processing involved?

additionalInformation.name: Collection
additionalInformation.description: Data subjects must also be informed on any `indirect' data collection, i.e. from third parties.

characteristic.name: Unawareness as a user sharing personal data
characteristic.description: The user does not need to be the data subject.

characteristicExample.name: Social media picture
characteristicExample.description: A user posting a picture on social media may not be aware that others in the picture are automatically tagged with a facial recognition system.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: Users that post a picture on social media may not be aware that they are also sharing personal data on the other individuals on their pictures.

characteristicExample.name: DNA testing service
characteristicExample.description: Using a DNA testing service can entail sharing medical information about family members.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: Using a DNA testing services can entail the sharing of sensitive medical information on family members. For example, the susceptability to certain types of genetic diseases.

characteristicExample.name: Address book sharing
characteristicExample.description: A service invites a user to share their address book to find contacts on a service.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: A service invites a user to share their address book to find contacts on a service. This entails the sharing of contact details and (part of ) the social network of the involved individuals.

impact.name: Unaware of impact on family or friends
impact.description: Users may not realize that they are unintentionally sharing personal data belonging to other individuals.

criteria.name: User unawareness
criteria.description: If a user shares personal data of others, is it clear what, why, and how that data is further processed?

additionalInformation.name: Sharing other people's data often omitted
additionalInformation.description: While users are often informed about the consequences of sharing their own data, systems rarely inform them about the impact of sharing data of others.

characteristic.name: Lack of data subject control
characteristic.description: Lack of control considers the lack of control of a data subject to choose and customize which, how, and how long personal data is processed.

characteristic.name: Preferences
characteristic.description: The lack of control of a data subject to set preferences or consent in how personal data is processed (or collected/stored).

characteristicExample.name: Sharing preferences
characteristicExample.description: The data subject is unable to set appropriate preferences on which data is shared and why.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: A site may not provide sufficiently detailed controls for data subjects to configure their privacy preferences on which of their data is shared and what types of processing can happen with that data.

characteristicExample.name: Consent
characteristicExample.description: The data subject is unable to set their consent preferences for the processing of personal data.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: The data subject is unable to give or revoke their consent for the processing of their personal data.

impact.name: Violation of data subject rights
impact.description: Appropriate control mechanisms are required to record data subject preferences and keep track of how the data may be further processed.
impact.fullDescription: Appropriate control mechanisms are required so that data subjects can accurately record their preferences and consent for the processing of their data. Without this you cannot accurately track what a data subject has consented to.

criteria.name: Lack of control
criteria.description: Does the system enable the data subject to configure which personal data is processed and for what purposes?

criteria.name: Alter afterwards
criteria.description: Can the data subject alter their preferences afterwards?

additionalInformation.name: Defaults
additionalInformation.description: Privacy-friendly settings should be the default.

additionalInformation.name: Nudging
additionalInformation.description: Nudging can raise awareness and induce more privacy-preserving behavior.

additionalInformation.name: Relevance
additionalInformation.description: Mainly relevant for systems directly collecting personal data from users.

characteristic.name: Access
characteristic.description: The lack of control in accessing the personal data that is being processed.

characteristicExample.name: Access processed data
characteristicExample.description: The data subject is unable to access their personal data held and processed by the service.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: While the data subject may be able to manage their preferences, they do not have access to what data is actually held and processed by the service.

characteristicExample.name: Wearable sensor data
characteristicExample.description: The sensor data from a wearable is transmitted to a lifestyle tracking app, but the user cannot access statistics and information derived from their data.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: Wearables, such as fitness trackers, collect detailed sensor data. The users, however, may be unable to get an overview of what data is collected and processed, and what information is derived from those data.

characteristicExample.name: No access mechanism
characteristicExample.description: It is not possible for a data subject to request access, neither directly through the system nor indirectly through a helpdesk.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: There is no access mechanism implemented for data subjects to requests access to their personal data. The access mechanism should be interpreted in the broad sense, so there is no automated way to request access, nor is there any manual process for the data subject to request access.

impact.name: Violation of data subject rights
impact.description: Lack of access may violate the legal rights of data subjects.
impact.fullDescription: Data subjects have a right of access to their personal data. Enabling access through the system ensures data subjects can exercise their rights without manual interventions.

criteria.name: Access to personal data
criteria.description: Do data subjects lack the ability to access the personal data being collected, processed, stored, or disclosed about them?

additionalInformation.name: Limitations
additionalInformation.description: The right to access is not always absolute. Limitations may exist depending on applicable laws (e.g., trade secrets, rights of other data subjects).

additionalInformation.name: Alternatives
additionalInformation.description: Access can also be obtained indirectly (e.g., a support ticket).

characteristic.name: Rectification/erasure
characteristic.description: The lack of control in rectifying incorrect data or removing personal data that is no longer relevant.

characteristicExample.name: Correct wrong data
characteristicExample.description: The data subject is unable to correct their personal data.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: The data subject is unable to modify incorrect personal data because the system only presents their personal data in a read-only way.

characteristicExample.name: Account not deleted
characteristicExample.description: When a data subject deletes their social media account, the account is disabled, but the actual data is not erased.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: The data subject is unable to delete their account. They can request the deletion of their account, but in practice their account remains present in a deactivated state.

characteristicExample.name: Address change
characteristicExample.description: A data subject is unable to update their home address after relocating.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: A data subject is unable to update their home address to a new address after having moved.

impact.name: Violation of data subject rights
impact.description: Data subjects have the right to rectify incorrect personal data or request the removal of data that is no longer relevant or needed.

criteria.name: Rectification or removal
criteria.description: Do data subjects have the ability to correct or delete their personal data?

additionalInformation.name: Alternatives
additionalInformation.description: Rectification or erasure can also be performed indirectly (e.g., through a customer service ticket).

impact.description: Unawareness and unintervenability are problematic because individuals are not informed about the potential implications of sharing personal data and cannot access or manage, withdraw, correct, or limit the processing.

additionalInformation.description: These threats may arise when there is (1) insufficient transparency (individuals are not aware of the collection or processing of their personal data or the personal data of others), (2) insufficient feedback (individuals are insufficiently informed about the privacy impact they may cause to others by using the system), and (3) insufficient intervenability (individuals cannot access or manage their personal data).

threatType.name: Non-compliance
threatType.description: Non-compliance threats arise when the system deviates from legislation, regulation, or standards and best practices, leading to the incomplete management of risk.
threatType.fullDescription: Privacy-related risks should not be focused upon in a vacuum, and a privacy risk assessment is ideally complemented with broader attention to broader risk perspectives, such as legal risk, and cybersecurity risk.

characteristic.name: Regulatory non-compliance
characteristic.description: There are legal consequences of the threats and/or processing activities described.
characteristic.fullDescription: The investigated data collection activities and/or the identified privacy threats are considered legally problematic in the context of the applicable regulatory framework.

characteristic.name: GDPR
characteristic.description: GDPR-related non-compliance threat characteristics
characteristic.fullDescription: This threat characteristic groups a number of relevant GDPR principles

characteristic.name: Insufficient data subject controls
characteristic.description: Support for the different data subject rights is lacking.
characteristic.fullDescription: Chapter 3 of GDPR codifies a wide range of intervenability and transparency requirements that should be implemented.

characteristic.name: Violation of data minimization principle
characteristic.description: More personal data is processed than is actually needed.
characteristic.fullDescription: Article 5.1(c) stipulates that

characteristicExample.name: Excessive personal data collected/processed
characteristicExample.description: The system collects or processes more data than is actually needed for the purposes of the processing.

characteristicExample.name: Web shop
characteristicExample.description: A web shop collects gender, phone number, date of birth, etc., while none of this information is necessary for billing.

impact.name: Data breach amplification
impact.description: Having more data than needed amplifies the impact of data breaches.

impact.name: GDPR
impact.description: Legislation such as the GDPR requires you not to process more than legally necessary for the processing.

criteria.name: Necessity data
criteria.description: Does the system collect or process more data than legally necessary?

additionalInformation.name: Purpose
additionalInformation.description: The purpose of your processing determines what data you are allowed to process.

characteristic.name: Unlawful processing of personal data
characteristic.description: Personal data is not processed in a lawful way
characteristic.fullDescription: Article 6 of GDPR codifies the conditions for lawful processing of personal data.

characteristic.name: Invalid consent
characteristic.description: Personal data collection and processing does not rely on valid consent.
characteristic.fullDescription: The constraints for valid consent are discussed in Art. 7

characteristicExample.name: Lack of consent management
characteristicExample.description: The processing relies on consent but there is no way for the data subject to give or revoke consent.

characteristicExample.name: Involuntary consent
characteristicExample.description: The consent is not freely given but forced. A user cannot access the service without giving consent.

impact.name: GDPR
impact.description: Legislation such as the GDPR imposes specific requirements for valid consent, not meeting these can result in heavy fines.

criteria.name: Consent requirements
criteria.description: Is the consent freely given, informed, specific, and unambiguous?

criteria.name: Withdrawable
criteria.description: Can consent be withdrawn?

criteria.name: Demonstrable
criteria.description: Can the consent be demonstrated?

additionalInformation.name: Consent not only lawful ground
additionalInformation.description: While frequently used, consent is not the only mechanism you can rely on. If you do rely on it, you need to meet the requirements for a having a valid consent.

characteristic.name: Lawfulness problems not related to consent
characteristic.description: Lawfulness problems not related to consent, such as incorrect lawful ground, automated decision making on sensitive personal data, etc.
characteristic.fullDescription: A wide range of lawfulness conditions are described in Art. 6.1(b-f)

characteristicExample.name: Smart TV
characteristicExample.description: A smart TV collects a user's viewing data without consent or any other lawful ground.

characteristicExample.name: Loan rejection
characteristicExample.description: A loan application is rejected without any possibility of human intervention.

characteristicExample.name: Automated-decision making
characteristicExample.description: A system makes automated decisions but relies on legitimate interest rather than explicit consent or contract.

impact.name: GDPR
impact.description: The GDPR imposes specific requirements for valid processing of personal data. Not meeting these can result in heavy fines.

criteria.name: Lawful ground
criteria.description: Does the collection rely on valid, appropriate lawful grounds for a specific purpose?

criteria.name: Automated decisions
criteria.description: Are there special types of processing such as automated decisions?

additionalInformation.name: AI/ML
additionalInformation.description: The use of machine learning techniques to process personal data or make decisions can impose additional requirements (e.g., transparency).

characteristic.name: Violation of storage limitation principle
characteristic.description: Personal data is stored longer than needed.
characteristic.fullDescription: Article 5.1(e) determines the principles regarding the maximal duration of retention.

characteristicExample.name: Stored longer than necessary
characteristicExample.description: Personal data is stored for a longer period than actually necessary to perform the processing.

characteristicExample.name: Old user accounts
characteristicExample.description: A website retains user account data long after users have closed their account and withdrawn their consent.

impact.name: Data breach amplification
impact.description: Having more data than needed amplifies the impact of data breaches.

impact.name: GDPR
impact.description: Legislation such as the GDPR requires you not to process more than legally necessary for the processing.

criteria.name: Necessity storage
criteria.description: Does the system store data longer than legally necessary?

additionalInformation.name: Purpose
additionalInformation.description: Purpose restrictions not only apply to processing but also to storage.

characteristic.name: Generic regulatory non-compliance
characteristic.description: A general description of non-compliance with regulations (non-specific to a particular legal regime or environment)

characteristicExample.name: No legal ground for processing under GDPR
characteristicExample.description: The system processes information of EU citizens without a valid legal ground under GDPR.

characteristicExample.name: Selling data in violation of the CCPA
characteristicExample.description: The system shares user information with third parties, violating 'Do Not Sell My Data' rights under the CCPA.

impact.name: Fines and sanctions
impact.description: Non-compliance with local regulations may lead to hefty fines or other sanctions.

impact.name: Reputational damage due to high-profile lawsuits
impact.description: High-profile complaint cases or lawsuits may lead to negative media exposure and reputational damage.

criteria.name: Jurisdiction with privacy laws
criteria.description: Will the system be used in jurisdictions with specific rules for personal data processing (e.g., the EU)?

criteria.name: System/processing does not adhere to applicable rules
criteria.description: Does the system, or its processing activities, violate one or more rules in these applicable regulation(s)?

additionalInformation.name: Perform a legal assessment
additionalInformation.description: Before processing any personal data, perform an assessment on the applicable regulations for your processing activities and system.

additionalInformation.name: Document how the system will adhere to applicable regulation
additionalInformation.description: Document how your system will adhere to the applicable legal framework and regularly check that this is still the case.

characteristic.name: Improper personal data management
characteristic.description: This characteristic groups a number of data management risks that may have privacy outcomes or vice versa, privacy threats that may lead to overarching data management problems.
characteristic.fullDescription: The management of personal data falls short, data management risks may include lack of holistic approaches or frameworks or more specifically, incomplete treatment of the data life-cycle (e.g. no automated deletion after a retention period)

characteristicExample.name: No principles for data retention
characteristicExample.description: There is no clear policy or mechanism to enforce deletion of data that is no longer needed.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: There is no policy or mechanism to define rules for data retention, archival and deletion within the system. This can lead to the system keeping data for longer than allowed, which poses a number of threats in the Data Disclosure threat type.

characteristicExample.name: No roles and responsibilities for data management defined
characteristicExample.description: The organizational roles and responsibilities surrounding data management in the system are not sufficiently defined.
characteristicExample.fullDescription: The organizational roles and responsibilities surrounding data management in the system are not sufficiently defined.

impact.name: Unmanaged data leading to privacy, security or availability issues
impact.description: Inadequate or nonexistent data lifecycle management can result in a loss of overview of the data within the system and its maintenance, posing concerns not only for privacy and data protection but also security and availability.

criteria.name: Data lifecycle management policy
criteria.description: Is there a data lifecycle management policy defined for the data processed within the system?

criteria.name: Clear data management principles for each lifecycle phase
criteria.description: Does the policy outline clear principles for each phase of the data lifecycle (creation, storage, sharing and usage, archival, and destruction)?

additionalInformation.name: Continuous review of the data lifecycle management
additionalInformation.description: Data lifecycle management is a continuous process that must be consistently carried out as long as the system is designed, developed, and used.

characteristic.name: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management
characteristic.description: A lack of proper cybersecurity risk management with specific attention to the interplay with privacy risks.
characteristic.fullDescription: A lack of proper cybersecurity risk management with specific attention to potential privacy consequences, or vice versa, privacy elements with cybersecurity implications (e.g. user data controls broadening the attack surface).

characteristicExample.name: No security assessment
characteristicExample.description: No security assessment was performed of the software.

characteristicExample.name: Operational security
characteristicExample.description: There are no processes in place to ensure software and services are kept up to date.

characteristicExample.name: Lacking internal access control mechanisms
characteristicExample.description: The organization does not use appropriate access control mechanisms to limit access of employees to personal data.

impact.name: Security contributes to privacy
impact.description: The security of the system plays a crucial role in safeguarding the privacy of individuals whose data is processed. Personal data breaches can result in significant fines and reputational damage.

criteria.name: Security process
criteria.description: Is there an established process to manage security risks and identify the required countermeasures?

criteria.name: Security countermeasures
criteria.description: Does the system incorporate the required countermeasures?

criteria.name: Process and countermeasures based on best practices
criteria.description: Are the countermeasures aligned with industry standards and best practices?

additionalInformation.name: STRIDE Threat Modeling
additionalInformation.description: Consider complementary methods like security threat modeling.

additionalInformation.name: Security standards
additionalInformation.description: Consider adhering to standards such as ISO27001 or the CIS Security Controls.

characteristic.name: Non-compliance with privacy standards and best practices

characteristicExample.name: ISO norm
characteristicExample.description: The system does not adhere to the best practices and principles outlined in the relevant ISO norms on data protection and privacy-by-design.

characteristicExample.name: NIST Privacy Framework
characteristicExample.description: Privacy risks are not classified and managed using a standardized methodology such as the NIST Privacy Framework.

elicitationCriteria.name: Non-compliance with privacy standards and best practices

impact.name: Demonstrating compliance
impact.description: Non-adherence to industry standards and best practices makes it more difficult to demonstrate compliance with applicable laws.

criteria.name: Privacy standards are applicable to the system
criteria.description: Are there any (industry) specific privacy standards that are applicable to the system?

criteria.name: System does not implement or violates applicable privacy standards
criteria.description: Does the system adequately implement the principles and controls outlined in these standards?

additionalInformation.name: Industry-specific guidance
additionalInformation.description: Check whether there is industry-specific guidance on data processing for your sector (e.g., healthcare, manufacturing).

impact.description: Violation of regulatory compliance obligations can lead to severe fines for the organization.

additionalInformation.description: When addressing potential privacy issues, also consider regulatory compliance, data lifecycle management, and cybersecurity risk. Pay specific attention to cases in which these aspects lead to privacy problems.
